tZh: Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 谈 AI、内容创作与离线生活
sEn: Adam Mosseri discusses AI content creators, tech bros' obsession with taste, and his explore page.
sZh: Adam Mosseri 讨论 AI 内容创作者、科技极客对品味的痴迷以及他的探索页面。

consensus.en: Reach is a means to an end, not the end itself; clarity of goal is essential.
consensus.zh: 触达是达到目的的手段，而非目的本身；明确目标至关重要。

consensus.en: Experimentation is key to growth; what works this year may not work next year.
consensus.zh: 实验是增长的关键；今年有效的方法明年可能失效。

consensus.en: Instagram's sweet spot is connecting people over shared interests, not just messaging or video.
consensus.zh: Instagram的强项是连接有共同兴趣的人，而不仅仅是消息或视频。

consensus.en: AI will increase the importance of knowing who is saying something and why, not just the content.
consensus.zh: AI将提升了解谁在说什么以及为何而说的重要性，而不仅仅是内容本身。

consensus.en: Creators should focus on building a smaller, influential following rather than chasing large numbers.
consensus.zh: 创作者应专注于建立较小但有影响力的粉丝群，而不是追逐大数字。

consensus.en: Transparency and control over the algorithm empower users and improve trust.
consensus.zh: 算法的透明度和控制权赋予用户力量并提升信任。

contrarian.en: Shadowbanning is a misconception; suppressing reach is not in Instagram's interest.
contrarian.zh: 影子封禁是误解；抑制触达不符合Instagram的利益。

contrarian.en: In a world of synthetic content, people will seek out human creators more, not less.
contrarian.zh: 在合成内容的世界里，人们会更寻求人类创作者，而非更少。

contrarian.en: Instagram is effectively the number one dating app, though it doesn't position itself as one.
contrarian.zh: Instagram实际上是第一大约会应用，尽管它不将自己定位为约会应用。

contrarian.en: Restrict is a powerful anti-bullying tool that provides plausible deniability for teens.
contrarian.zh: 限制是一个强大的反欺凌工具，为青少年提供合理的否认空间。

contrarian.en: AI can help identify policy-violating content more accurately, reducing false positives.
contrarian.zh: AI能更准确地识别违反政策的内容，减少误报。

contrarian.en: Tech bros' obsession with taste is a humanizing differentiator in an AI-driven world.
contrarian.zh: 科技兄弟对品味的痴迷是AI驱动世界中人性的差异化因素。

turns.zh: 但双因素认证，你是双因素认证的倡导者。

turns.en: Two-factor, no SMS.
turns.zh: 双因素认证，别用短信。

turns.en: Okay. Because if you do get hacked and you become part of this farm, your account just gets nuked. You're annihilated once we sniff you out.
turns.zh: 好的。因为如果你真的被黑，成了这种农场的一部分，你的账号就会被炸掉。一旦我们嗅到你，你就完了。

turns.en: Yes. Well, if you lose your account.
turns.zh: 是的。嗯，如果你丢了账号。

turns.en: Yeah. Well, if it's a big account, they might start posting things they're trying to promote. But they don't usually do that because then you'd report it and it'd get taken down. So what they do is they just like stuff on your behalf and follow stuff on your behalf that you don't even necessarily notice, but they're selling those likes elsewhere. And now your account's kind of...
turns.zh: 是啊。嗯，如果是大号，他们可能会开始发一些他们想推广的内容。但他们通常不会这么做，因为那样你会举报，然后账号会被封。所以他们只是用你的名义点赞、关注，你甚至不一定注意到，但他们把这些点赞卖到别处。现在你的账号就有点……

turns.en: I wonder the biggest celeb who fell for this, and it's like, 'Wow, Tom Cruise just liked my FitPic. Thank god I spent a thousand bucks, dude. Hell yeah.'
turns.zh: 我好奇哪个最大的名人上过这种当，就像：“哇，汤姆·克鲁斯刚赞了我的健身照。谢天谢地我花了一千美元，老兄。太棒了。”

turns.en: It's not good.
turns.zh: 这可不好。

turns.en: What's the vibe like in the Bay? You're in the Bay.
turns.zh: 湾区氛围怎么样？你在湾区。

turns.en: Yes, I'm in San Francisco.
turns.zh: 是的，我在旧金山。

turns.en: What's the vibe like in the Bay Area now that AI is proliferating?
turns.zh: 现在 AI 遍地开花，湾区氛围怎么样？

turns.en: It's in the cars.
turns.zh: 它就在车里。

turns.en: There are a lot of billboards.
turns.zh: 有很多广告牌。

turns.en: A lot of AI billboards.
turns.zh: 很多 AI 广告牌。

turns.en: How analog.
turns.zh: 好复古。

turns.en: The Bay Area is a weird place. I love the Bay. I've been in San Francisco since 2005. There are people who hate on it.
turns.zh: 湾区是个奇怪的地方。我爱湾区。我从 2005 年就住在旧金山。有人讨厌它。

turns.en: You got hyphy.
turns.zh: 你嗨起来了。

turns.en: Yeah. You ghost ride the whip, dude.
turns.zh: 是啊。你幽灵漂移，兄弟。

turns.en: No, but it was cool because in those first couple years, we were the first ones to have Airbnb. We were the first ones to have Uber. It kind of felt like you were living in the future a little bit.
turns.zh: 不，但那很酷，因为在那最初几年，我们最先有了 Airbnb，最先有了 Uber。感觉有点像活在未来。

turns.en: It's not a perfect city by any means, but it's also not the apocalypse that people make it out to be, right?
turns.zh: 它绝不是一座完美的城市，但也不是人们说的那种末日景象，对吧？

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: I like being there because for what I do, it's sort of the center. I also like that we get access to things early. Like, I like Waymos.
turns.zh: 我喜欢待在那里，因为对我做的事来说，那里算是中心。我也喜欢我们能提前用到新东西。比如，我喜欢 Waymo。

turns.en: Really? I love Waymos.
turns.zh: 真的吗？我爱 Waymo。

turns.en: What about when they get in a self-propagated traffic jam in a parking lot?
turns.zh: 那它们在停车场里造成自传播堵车怎么办？

turns.en: Self-propagated traffic jam. I'll tell you the second time I got into a Waymo.
turns.zh: 自传播堵车。我跟你说我第二次坐 Waymo 的经历。

turns.en: They won me over. I sit in the front because the first time...
turns.zh: 它们把我征服了。我坐前排，因为第一次……

turns.en: Yeah. Well, no. Because the first time you were just like, 'What's happening? There's like a ghost driver. The thing is turning and there's no one turning the wheel.'
turns.zh: 是啊。嗯，不。因为第一次你就像：“怎么回事？有个幽灵司机。车在转弯，但没人打方向盘。”

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: So I was like, 'All right.'
turns.zh: 所以我就想：“好吧。”

turns.en: Ghost drivers in all these parts.
turns.zh: 到处都是幽灵司机。

turns.en: Yeah. So I don't want to be like Driving Miss Daisy, ghost driver style. So I sat shotgun the second time.
turns.zh: 是啊。所以我不想像《为黛西小姐开车》那样，幽灵司机风格。所以第二次我坐了副驾。

turns.en: And I'm sitting shotgun and we hit a yellow light.
turns.zh: 我坐在副驾，然后我们遇到黄灯。

turns.en: And I'm like, 'Oh, all right, Ghost Driver, what are you going to do?'
turns.zh: 然后我想：“哦，好吧，幽灵司机，你要怎么办？”

turns.en: What are you going to do? The ultimate test, pop quiz.
turns.zh: 你要怎么办？终极测试，突击测验。

turns.en: Yeah. What's your deal? Are you a brake guy? Are you a slam-on-the-gas guy?
turns.zh: 是啊。你怎么处理？你是踩刹车派，还是猛踩油门派？

turns.en: And it didn't do either. It did the math and just cruised right through. It's like, 'All right, 33 miles an hour, 120 yards, we're good.' And just cruised at the same speed.
turns.zh: 它两个都没做。它算了算，然后直接匀速通过。就像：“好了，时速 33 英里，120 码，没问题。”然后保持原速通过。

turns.en: And a human can't do that.
turns.zh: 人类做不到。

turns.en: No. And I was like, 'All right, you could drive me to work every day. I'm sold.'
turns.zh: 不。然后我想：“好吧，你可以每天送我上班。我服了。”

turns.en: Can you get on the aux in Waymos?
turns.zh: 在 Waymo 里能连 AUX 吗？

turns.en: I don't know.
turns.zh: 我不知道。

turns.en: Or Bluetooth, I guess, because there's no...
turns.zh: 或者蓝牙，我猜，因为没有……

turns.en: Yeah, you can. You control the audio now. That's actually... No, I forgot that you can.
turns.zh: 可以，你能。现在你可以控制音频。其实……不，我忘了你可以。

turns.en: Are you allowed to drink in them?
turns.zh: 在里面能喝酒吗？

turns.en: I really hope not.
turns.zh: 我真希望不能。

turns.en: Probably open container. Probably not.
turns.zh: 可能算开放式容器。可能不行。

turns.en: Ask for a friend. Ask for a friend. Exactly.
turns.zh: 帮朋友问的。帮朋友问的。没错。

turns.en: But is everyone like evangelizing? 'I go AI.'
turns.zh: 但每个人都在传道吗？“我搞 AI。”

turns.en: No, there's both. There are people... Look, I think too much of this debate around AI is either the total zealot AI pill crew or the really intense doomer sort of apocalypse crew.
turns.zh: 不，两种都有。有人……你看，我觉得关于 AI 的争论，太多要么是彻底的 AI 狂热派，要么是强烈的末日派。

turns.en: That's the two camps, right?
turns.zh: 就是这两个阵营，对吧？

turns.en: Yeah. But I just think there's a lot of nuance. There's a lot of room in the middle, and there's not enough people talking about it. There are real risks. There is a lot of change. It's going to happen real fast. It's going to be hard for us to digest. There are also amazing opportunities and amazing things that it can help us do. And that's already happening.
turns.zh: 是啊。但我只是觉得有很多细微差别。中间有很大空间，但谈论的人不够多。存在真实的风险。会有很多变化。会来得很快。我们很难消化。但也有惊人的机遇和它能帮我们做到的惊人事情。而且这已经在发生了。

turns.en: This isn't necessarily a sexy or exciting thing, but I'm actually very excited about it. One of the things we're finding with AI models is that we're way better at finding content that violates our rules without catching content that doesn't. Because to us, the more we push on finding more of the bad stuff, we inevitably have what we call false positives. So taking down things that we shouldn't, that sucks. No one wants that.
turns.zh: 这不一定是什么性感或令人兴奋的事，但我其实非常兴奋。我们通过 AI 模型发现的一件事是，我们更擅长找出违反规则的内容，而不会误伤合规内容。因为对我们来说，越是努力去找出更多坏内容，就不可避免地会出现我们所谓的误报。所以下架那些不该下架的东西，那很糟糕。没人想要那样。

turns.en: So it sounds like there is a nipple team.
turns.zh: 所以听起来有一个“乳头团队”。

turns.en: Yeah, they have it on their business cards.
turns.zh: 是啊，他们的名片上就印着这个。

turns.en: Do you use AI in your personal life at all?
turns.zh: 你在个人生活中会使用 AI 吗？

turns.en: Yeah, all the time. I tend to build for me. What do I use it for? I've built a bunch of apps that I just use in my daily life.
turns.zh: 会，一直都在用。我倾向于为自己构建东西。我用它做什么？我建了一堆日常使用的应用。

turns.en: Just for you, for the house? Build apps just for you, for Adam?
turns.zh: 就为你自己，为家里？就为亚当建应用？

turns.en: Yeah, I just have a bunch of these like fresh-baked software. I have like three or four apps I just use every day that I built.
turns.zh: 对，我有一堆这种“新鲜出炉”的软件。我建了三四个应用，每天都会用。

turns.en: Sick. Damn. Any of those sellable?
turns.zh: 太酷了。天哪。那些能卖吗？

turns.en: I mean maybe, but I don't. I'm not going to do that. For me, there is a world in which eventually AI is going to be able to create interfaces for you or software for you on the fly so quickly that you know what is Instagram in a world where it can adapt the UI, not just the content, to your interests. So I wanted to make sure I play around in that space. I built one for health. I've got one for just tracking my packages. I can build a bunch of little things.
turns.zh: 也许可以，但我不打算那样做。对我来说，未来 AI 将能够如此迅速地为你即时创建界面或软件，以至于在它能根据你的兴趣调整界面而不仅仅是内容的世界里，Instagram 会变成什么样。所以我想确保自己在这个领域有所探索。我建了一个健康类的，还有一个跟踪包裹的。我可以建很多小东西。

turns.en: How much are these clothing packages you're buying?
turns.zh: 你买的这些衣服包裹多少钱？

turns.en: Yeah, it's mostly CDLP underwear, personal linen shirts.
turns.zh: 主要是 CDLP 内裤，个人亚麻衬衫。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And my kids' sports stuff.
turns.zh: 还有我孩子的运动装备。

turns.en: But I use it for writing. I don't have it write for me. I write a lot both internally and externally. So I'll write something and then I will ask it for vicious critique. Particularly Claude. Claude really doesn't hold back. Particularly mean.
turns.zh: 但我用它来写作。我不会让它替我写。我写很多东西，无论是内部还是外部。所以我写完一些东西后，会请它给出犀利的批评。尤其是 Claude，它真的毫不留情，特别刻薄。

turns.en: Yeah, in a way I kind of appreciate that. Claude is for writing, but it's actually great.
turns.zh: 是啊，某种程度上我挺欣赏这一点。Claude 是用于写作的，但它确实很棒。

turns.en: For a long time, I haven't done this now because they're a little older. For a long time, when ChatGPT first came out, I would, when I read books to my kids at bedtime, I would always end with, 'All right, you pick a protagonist, you pick a context, you pick a theme.' And they'd be like, 'All right, I want a shark named Robot who is in a race.' So I'd make a prompt. I'd be like, 'I need a five-minute story for an 8-year-old about a shark named Robot in a race where the moral of the story is to listen to your father as Bandit would do.' And then I read it and they loved it.
turns.zh: 很长一段时间，我现在不这么做了，因为他们大一点了。很长一段时间，当 ChatGPT 刚出来时，我给孩子读睡前故事，总会以“好了，你选一个主角，你选一个背景，你选一个主题”结尾。他们会说“好，我想要一条叫罗伯特的鲨鱼参加比赛”。然后我会写一个提示词，比如“我需要一个给 8 岁孩子的五分钟故事，关于一条叫罗伯特的鲨鱼参加比赛，故事寓意是要像班迪特那样听父亲的话”。然后我读给他们听，他们很喜欢。

turns.en: Okay. Do you say thank you to Claude?
turns.zh: 好的。你会对 Claude 说谢谢吗？

turns.en: I do. I think it's important. Maybe not in your writing, but this is true for a long time with Alexa. I have little kids. If you just bark orders at Alexa like 'What time is it?' No.
turns.zh: 我会。我觉得这很重要。也许不是在写作中，但长期以来对 Alexa 也是如此。我有小孩。如果你只是对 Alexa 吼命令，比如“现在几点？”不。

turns.en: Yeah, they learn by most.
turns.zh: 是啊，他们主要通过模仿学习。

turns.en: No, they're not thinking about it. Play E40.
turns.zh: 不，他们不会想那么多。播放 E40。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: So I say please and I say thank you.
turns.zh: 所以我会说“请”和“谢谢”。

turns.en: Play E40, please.
turns.zh: 请播放 E40。

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. Because that way it helps.
turns.zh: 对，就是这样。因为这样有帮助。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: As fashion and tech become so intertwined, what are some positive things you think will come from this ever more involved, intertwined relationship?
turns.zh: 随着时尚和科技变得如此紧密，你认为这种越来越紧密的关系会带来哪些积极的东西？

turns.en: Well, I think you said it: this unholy marriage.
turns.zh: 嗯，我想你说过：这种不神圣的结合。

turns.en: You said it. You said it. We're not really known for our fashion sense. Talk about that.
turns.zh: 你说的。你说的。我们并不以时尚感著称。谈谈这个。

turns.en: Yeah, we should definitely talk about that. One of the reasons why I actually really love what I do is because part of what platforms like Instagram do is they allow anyone with taste and something interesting to say to actually find an audience. And the fact that you've got people like Xander, who's a substitute middle school teacher in somewhere middle America, has a passionate following is just a rad thing that couldn't have existed.
turns.zh: 是的，我们绝对应该谈谈这个。我真正热爱我所做的事情的原因之一是，像 Instagram 这样的平台允许任何有品味、有有趣内容的人真正找到受众。像 Xander 这样的人，他是美国中西部某地的代课中学老师，却拥有热情的追随者，这真是太酷了，这在以前是不可能存在的。

turns.en: That's true. Sure. Yeah.
turns.zh: 确实如此。当然。嗯。

turns.en: So to me, that's the good stuff.
turns.zh: 所以对我来说，这就是好的部分。

turns.en: And the bad stuff?
turns.zh: 那坏的部分呢？

turns.en: Well, I don't know, Adidas sandals and flip flops. There's the tech bro uniform.
turns.zh: 嗯，我不知道，阿迪达斯凉鞋和人字拖。还有科技兄弟的制服。

turns.en: If we go back far enough on your IG, will we see you wearing the tech bro uniform?
turns.zh: 如果我们翻你 Instagram 足够久，会看到你穿科技兄弟制服吗？

turns.en: I don't think you'll see a tech bro uniform, but you'll probably see something bad.
turns.zh: 我觉得你不会看到科技兄弟制服，但可能会看到一些糟糕的东西。

turns.en: Some for sure. Oh, yeah.
turns.zh: 肯定有。哦，是的。

turns.en: That's everyone though, right? You got to try stuff.
turns.zh: 但每个人都是这样，对吧？你得尝试各种东西。

turns.en: I agree. What have I tried that's bad?
turns.zh: 我同意。我试过什么糟糕的？

turns.en: I don't know. I look back and I'm sure in the 2000s my pants were way too tight.
turns.zh: 我不知道。我回头看，肯定在 2000 年代我的裤子太紧了。

turns.en: We went through a lot of that. Some joggers maybe. Yeah.
turns.zh: 我们经历了很多那种。也许有些慢跑裤。嗯。

turns.en: Were you ever of the generation that was wearing hoodie and flip-flops to the office?
turns.zh: 你是属于穿连帽衫和人字拖去办公室的那一代吗？

turns.en: No, I wasn't. But when I moved out to San Francisco in '05, and when I started working at Facebook in '08, that was kind of the uniform. But I was much more like black boots and jeans and a black t-shirt.
turns.zh: 不，我不是。但当我 2005 年搬到旧金山，2008 年开始在 Facebook 工作时，那算是制服。但我更倾向于黑色靴子、牛仔裤和黑色 T 恤。

turns.en: Dress for the job you want, New York.
turns.zh: 为你想做的工作而着装，纽约。

turns.en: I was like, 'Ah, I got to react to this California style.'
turns.zh: 我当时想，“啊，我得对加州风格做出反应。”

turns.en: Yeah, I'm going to overreact like a mixologist and show all of them.
turns.zh: 是啊，我要像调酒师一样反应过度，给他们看看。

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. It was not interesting. But that was definitely the uniform for a bit.
turns.zh: 对，就是这样。那并不有趣。但确实有一段时间那是制服。

turns.en: What's the tech bro uniform in 2026? Because we don't know.
turns.zh: 2026 年科技兄弟的制服是什么？因为我们不知道。

turns.en: I don't know. It's not as consistent now, right? Because now you've got the world of quiet luxury where you've got these guys with these $1,200 sneakers or whatever. Or Piana. But it's not the same. The Apple uniform is a uniform. So there's the Steve Jobs-inspired simplicity thing, but then the Apple designers kind of have their own vibe, which is a little bit higher-end brands.
turns.zh: 我不知道。现在不那么一致了，对吧？因为现在有“安静奢华”的世界，那些家伙穿着 1200 美元的 sneakers 之类的。或者 Piana。但不一样了。苹果的制服是制服。所以有受乔布斯启发的简约风格，但苹果设计师们有自己的风格，偏向高端品牌。

turns.en: Can you kind of clock someone by their fit? Like if you're at a restaurant, 'Oh yeah, that guy works for Uber' or 'That guy's an engineer'?
turns.zh: 你能通过穿着认出某人吗？比如在餐厅里，“哦，那家伙在 Uber 工作”或“那家伙是工程师”？

turns.en: A little bit. Yeah, a little bit. It depends on the company. Like Uber, no. But Apple design, yeah.
turns.zh: 有一点。是的，有一点。取决于公司。比如 Uber，不会。但苹果设计，会。

turns.en: But um but yeah, I don't think like if you look at the big tech titans, right, if you look at like Satia and like Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg and Sundar, like they you know, they don't have a quite as quite as consistent a look.
turns.zh: 但是，嗯，是的，我不认为，如果你看看那些科技巨头，对吧，如果你看看萨蒂亚、杰夫·贝索斯、马克·扎克伯格和桑达尔，他们你知道，他们的风格并不那么一致。

turns.en: I mean, are you the kind of the resident like swaggy exec? Like how often does Mark ask you to uh you know, or does he consult you before he drops a Fitbit?
turns.zh: 我的意思是，你是那种常驻的、有范儿的高管吗？比如马克多久会问你一次，嗯，你知道，或者他在戴 Fitbit 之前会咨询你吗？

turns.en: No, he yo yo, which one?
turns.zh: 不，他哟哟，哪一个？

turns.en: Yeah, he does not the one you like best.
turns.zh: 是的，他不是你最喜欢的那一个。

turns.en: does not consult me before he drops a fit. That would be amazing though in front of my job.
turns.zh: 他在戴 Fitbit 之前不会咨询我。不过那在我工作面前会很棒。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: He's like, "What should I wear?"
turns.zh: 他会说：“我该穿什么？”

turns.en: Um, no. I mean, look, I mean, I I we have our leadership team has got a from a bunch of different parts of a bunch of different industries at this point with a bunch of different types of experiences. People think of me as more closer to fashion. Just cuz I'm at Instagram
turns.zh: 嗯，不。我的意思是，你看，我是说，我们领导团队来自不同行业的不同领域，拥有各种不同的经验。人们认为我更接近时尚，只是因为我在 Instagram。

turns.en: and you go to the Met Gala, that doesn't hurt. Yeah. But also, that's true. That fits off.
turns.zh: 而且你去参加 Met Gala，那也不无帮助。是的。但这也是事实。那很合适。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. I mean, look at you.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。我的意思是，看看你。

turns.en: And like smaller designers, too. Like not

turns.zh: 80 岁的时候，你能做“环游世界喝酒”吗？

turns.zh: 我喜欢你们有，我是说，就是那个你们拍照的镜子，对吧？

turns.zh: 那是我们的特色。那是我们的 IG 时刻。
